speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old female. The patient presents with a 5-day history of severe abdominal pain and cramping, accompanied by nausea and vomiting. She reports pain with urination and also experienced burning pain during sexual intercourse 3 days ago. She mentions being sexually active with one male partner, using condoms inconsistently.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID) secondary to Chlamydia trachomatis or Neisseria gonorrhoeae.

The patient is a sexually active 17-year-old female with a 5-day history of severe lower abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and dysuria. She reports dyspareunia (pain with sexual intercourse) three days ago and inconsistent condom use. These findings are highly suggestive of an ascending genital infection causing PID, possibly complicated by a tubo-ovarian abscess or appendicitis.

Given the severity of symptoms (vomiting, severe pain) and the high pre-test probability of PID, immediate evaluation is required.
REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis and Urine Culture to rule out cystitis and pyelonephritis.
REQUEST TEST: Pregnancy test (beta-hCG) to rule out ectopic pregnancy.
REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential and CRP to assess for infection/sepsis.
